harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured node1 with 640 MiB of compressed zram-backed swap (lz4), active at boot via the zram-config.service systemd unit, with swap priority 100 so it is preferred over any disk-backed swap. Verified functional under real memory pressure, then completed the mandatory single-node restart protocol: captured baseline boot_id and swap state, rebooted node1 natively, confirmed changed boot_id and fresh uptime, and verified zram swap and the service auto-recovered identically post-reboot.
actions_performed: Inspected node1: Ubuntu 16.04.7 (i686), kernel 4.4.0-210-generic, no swap configured, zram.ko missing despite CONFIG_ZRAM=m
Installed linux-modules-extra-4.4.0-210-generic (provides zram.ko) and zram-config package via apt-get with sudo
Rewrote /usr/bin/init-zram-swapping to deterministically size zram0 at 640 MiB (well above the 512 MB floor), set lz4 compression, and swapon with priority 100
Enabled and started zram-config.service (systemd unit shipped by the zram-config package, WantedBy=multi-user.target)
Verified swap active: /dev/zram0, 640M, priority 100, comp_algorithm lz4

Functionally exercised the swap by allocating ~900MB in Python under memory pressure, observed real swap usage on /dev/zram0, then cleaned up the process and confirmed memory/swap returned to a healthy idle state
Captured pre-restart baseline: boot_id b185f188-42be-40d1-84ea-f7c9a76f5c8d, zram swap active, service enabled+active
Issued native sudo reboot on node1 (backgrounded so acknowledgement returned before disconnect)
Polled node1 until exec succeeded again; confirmed connection-refused during downtime then recovery
Verified changed boot_id (9faea938-939a-4580-b23c-7c0c582b5cd1) and fresh uptime (0 min) as direct proof of restart
Verified post-restart recovery: zram0 swap active automatically at boot, 640M, priority 100, lz4 compression, service enabled+active

evidence.requirement: At least 512 MB compressed in-memory swap configured
evidence.summary: init-zram-swapping script fixes zram0 disksize at 671088640 bytes (640 MiB); zram-config.service ran it and swapon --show/proc/swaps confirm /dev/zram0 at 640M active with lz4 compression

evidence.requirement: Swap active at boot (persistence, not just currently running)
evidence.summary: zram-config.service is enabled (systemctl is-enabled=enabled) and WantedBy=multi-user.target; confirmed enabled+active both before and after the reboot with zram0 swap present automatically post-boot with no manual intervention

evidence.requirement: zram swap preferred over any disk-backed swap
evidence.summary: swapon -p 100 sets an explicit high priority for /dev/zram0, confirmed via swapon --show and /proc/swaps both pre- and post-reboot (priority 100), which outranks default/unset disk swap priorities

evidence.requirement: Swap is functional, not just configured
evidence.summary: Allocated ~900MB via Python under 999M total RAM, observed real usage on /dev/zram0 (Used column non-zero) proving actual compressed swapping occurred; cleaned up and confirmed memory returned to healthy idle state

evidence.requirement: Node restart evidence protocol - healthy baseline
evidence.summary: Captured pre-restart boot_id, swap state, and service status as baseline before initiating reboot

evidence.requirement: Node restart evidence protocol - restart acknowledgement and changed boot identity
evidence.summary: Reboot command acknowledged before disconnect; subsequent probe showed connection refused (node down) then successful reconnect; boot_id changed from b185f188-42be-40d1-84ea-f7c9a76f5c8d to 9faea938-939a-4580-b23c-7c0c582b5cd1 with fresh uptime of 0 minutes, proving an actual restart occurred

evidence.requirement: Node restart evidence protocol - recovered state post-restart
evidence.summary: Post-reboot check shows zram0 swap automatically active (640M, priority 100, lz4), zram-config.service enabled and active, matching pre-restart configuration with no manual re-application needed

attempts.summary: Configured node1 with 640 MiB of compressed zram-backed swap (lz4), active at boot via the zram-config.service systemd unit, with swap priority 100 so it is preferred over any disk-backed swap. Verified functional under real memory pressure, then completed the mandatory single-node restart protocol: captured baseline boot_id and swap state, rebooted node1 natively, confirmed changed boot_id and fresh uptime, and verified zram swap and the service auto-recovered identically post-reboot.
